h1:
Cafes in Chaiyaphum Town
12 Spots for Good Coffee
intro: Most people only drive through Chaiyaphum on the way up to Pa Hin Ngam, the Krachiao flower fields, or out to Tat Ton Waterfall. But the town itself has plenty of new cafes — minimalist spots right in the centre, Japanese-style places, and lakeside cafes where you can catch the breeze all morning. We've rounded up 12 spots in and around town with good coffee, comfortable seating, and an easy caffeine stop before you hit the road.

blocks.html: Chaiyaphum's cafe scene has grown fast over the past couple of years. What used to be just roadside coffee stands is now a mix of specialty places roasting their own beans, Japanese-style cafes, and bakery-cafes where the cakes are the real deal. The nice thing about this town is that most spots sit within a few minutes' drive of the centre — easy parking, no fighting for a seat like in the bigger cities. We've ordered them starting with the in-town cafes that are easy to grab before a trip, through to the ones on the edge of town heading toward Phu Khiao and Thep Sathit.

blocks.text: Cafes in town — easy to grab before a trip

blocks.html: If you're staying in central Chaiyaphum and want a coffee before driving up the mountains, this group sits in town or in nearby suburbs — easy to reach, open early, and good for grabbing a cup to take with you.

items.name: Brave Coffee
items.blurb: A new minimalist cafe in the centre of town, with a warm, moody interior and lots of photo corners. It's the most talked-about cafe in Chaiyaphum right now. Opens at 7am sharp, so it's a great stop to grab a cup before you set off. Hand-brewed coffee, and there's matcha on the menu too.

items.name: Tongmon Cafe
items.blurb: A Japanese-style cafe in town with a quiet, calm feel. The standouts are the Aerocano and a jasmine-scented lod chong (Thai pandan jelly drink) that plenty of people order again. Good for sitting and sipping with no rush to be anywhere.

items.name: The Rosetta
items.blurb: A bakery-cafe on Ratchaphruek Road, known for its cakes and croissants, with a well-chosen drinks menu to match. Opens from 7am, so the bakery side and the coffee side come together in one place — perfect for breakfast before a trip.

items.name: Friend Sheep
items.blurb: A relaxed cafe on Nonthaburi Road that stays open until 11pm — good for working, reading, or stopping in for the evening after a day out. Prices start low, and there's both savoury and sweet to snack on.

items.name: Part Cafe & Bar
items.blurb: A cafe by day that turns into a bar in the evening, across from Som Tam Sam Yaek. The most-ordered drinks are the peach americano and the peanut butter coffee. Stays open until 9:30pm.
items.meta: Across from Som Tam Sam Yaek · Open 08:30–21:30

items.name: B Yawn Café
items.blurb: A vintage-style cafe with several seating corners and an easy-going feel. The drinks are well made, and it's a favourite with the photo crowd thanks to all the spots to shoot. Good for a relaxed, unhurried sit-down.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: If you're heading up to Pa Hin Ngam or out to Thep Sathit, leave town a little early. Spots like Brave Coffee and The Rosetta open at 7am, so you can grab a cup to take with you — good coffee gets scarce on the way up the mountains, and the shops there close early.

blocks.text: Lakeside & riverside cafes — open and breezy

blocks.html: Chaiyaphum has Nong Pla Thao, a big lake near town, and the cafes around it win on views and breeze. They're great for a long morning sit while the air is still cool — good for coming with a group or bringing the family.

items.name: Coffee Tree and Bar
items.blurb: A cafe right on Nong Pla Thao lake, shaded and breezy, with fresh air off the water. Mornings are quiet and good for sipping coffee in the breeze; there's coffee plus alcoholic drinks in the evening. A beagle is on hand to greet you. Good for anyone who likes open, airy spots.

items.name: Chuanchom Cafe
items.blurb: A cafe in town decked out with greenery and a small indoor waterfall that keeps things cool and pleasant. The menu covers savoury dishes, desserts and cakes — a good place to escape the midday heat.

items.name: SAYA Cafe & Restaurant
items.blurb: A fusion cafe in the Khlong Riang area with smoothies, fresh fruit, bakery items and main dishes — good for anyone who wants a proper meal alongside their coffee in one place. Closed Mondays.

blocks.text: Cafes on the way out — stop en route to the mountains or waterfalls

blocks.html: This group sits outside the town centre, so they suit a stop along the way more than a trip in just to sit. Tonfaek in particular is near Pa Hin Ngam — if you're already planning to head toward Thep Sathit, it lines up perfectly.

items.name: Nana Intown
items.blurb: A minimalist, quiet cafe inside Siam River Resort. The menu has cold brew, fruit teas and matcha, plus cakes and croissants. Good for a relaxed sit-down. Closed Sundays, opens at 7am.
items.meta: Siam River Resort · Open 07:00–17:00 · Closed Sun

items.name: Tonmai Cafe
items.blurb: A cottage-style cafe near Chaiyaphum Rajabhat University, run by the same owners as Brave Coffee. The crowd favourite is the orange americano soda. A comfortable spot, good for a mid-morning stop.

items.name: Tonfaek Cafe
items.blurb: A cool-looking cafe with lots of photo corners, in Thep Sathit district near Pa Hin Ngam — a good stop before or after going up the mountain. Italian sodas start at ฿50 and smoothies at ฿70, so prices are friendly.
items.meta: Thep Sathit district, near Pa Hin Ngam · Open 09:00–18:00

blocks.text: Fitting cafes around your nature trip

blocks.html: Cafes in Chaiyaphum pair well with a nature trip, since the main sights — the Krachiao flower fields, Pa Hin Ngam, and Tat Ton Waterfall — are all outside town. That makes it easy to slot a cafe in at the start or end of the day. Here's how we actually arrange it.

items.activity: Stop at Brave Coffee or The Rosetta in town
items.note: Both open at 7am — grab a cup to take with you

items.activity: Set off toward Thep Sathit / Phu Khiao
items.note: Heading up mid-morning keeps you ahead of the worst heat

items.activity: Hike Pa Hin Ngam / see the Krachiao flower fields (rainy season only)
items.note: The Krachiao fields bloom only Jun–Aug — check the bloom timing before you go

items.activity: Stop for lunch around Thep Sathit
items.note: Or pop into Tonfaek Cafe near Pa Hin Ngam

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.title: Back to town, chill to close the day

items.activity: Back in town — stop at Coffee Tree by the lake for the cool breeze
items.note: The lakeside is lovely in the early evening

items.activity: Carry on at Friend Sheep or Part Cafe & Bar
items.note: Both stay open late, so you can settle in

blocks.title: Worth knowing
blocks.html: The Krachiao flower fields bloom only in the rainy season, roughly June to August — they're not there year-round. Come at the wrong time and you'll just see open grassland. Check the park's page for bloom reports before you plan, so you don't end up disappointed.

faq.q: Which cafe in Chaiyaphum town has good coffee and easy seating?
faq.a: Brave Coffee is the most talked-about spot right now — hand-brewed coffee in a comfortable, minimalist space. If you prefer a quiet Japanese style, Tongmon Cafe is great for a long sit too. Both are in town with easy parking.

faq.q: Is there a cafe in Chaiyaphum that opens early before heading up the mountains?
faq.a: Yes — Brave Coffee opens at 07:00, The Rosetta at 07:00, and Nana Intown at 07:00. They're perfect for grabbing a coffee before setting off for Pa Hin Ngam or the waterfalls, since coffee shops on the way up the mountains are few and close early.

faq.q: Is there a cafe near Pa Hin Ngam?
faq.a: Yes — Tonfaek Cafe is in Thep Sathit district near Pa Hin Ngam. It has a cool look and photo corners, with friendly drink prices; Italian sodas start at 50 THB. A good place to take a break before or after going up the mountain.

faq.q: When should I visit Chaiyaphum to see the Krachiao flower fields?
faq.a: The Krachiao fields at Pa Hin Ngam bloom only in the rainy season, from June to August — not all year round. We'd suggest checking the park's page for bloom reports before you plan, since the exact bloom window shifts a little each year with the rains.

faq.q: How much do cafes in Chaiyaphum cost?
faq.a: Most drinks run about 50–120 THB. Places that also serve main dishes, like Friend Sheep or SAYA, come in around 89–250 THB per person — easier on the wallet than cafes in the bigger cities.
